summary: load_outcomes was half a reader: the dataclass exclusion half was missing
The whole introspect differential reported ok in 0.011s: pyprobe.Marker was 'src/introspect.py' where the helper wants a path relative to src/, so every probe took the honest source-unavailable SKIP
Deleting the is_error gate from the hallucination scan survived a 37-mutant battery because every fixture carrying 'No such tool available' also carried is_error true

A len(want)==0 && len(got)==0 early return normalized nil-vs-empty away and was the only reason a return-nil-for-clean-transcript mutant survived; json.dumps([]) is [] and a nil Go slice marshals to null into a shared store
Aliasing worstNames to the live streak is unkillable in Go because the reset branch is = nil; only the pair (truncation reset AND alias) is observable, so the mutant had to become a two-part edit
estimate_cost's max(0,min(cache,tokens_in)) clamps commute for every tokens_in>=0, so swapping them is invisible to any plausible fixture; they part only on a negative input count
matchesLookUp's doc comment still claimed the words list carried the two common look-up spellings after those spellings were removed from it
A 30-case CPython-per-case mint probe left by the r4 reviewer took 14 min and blew the 10-minute package timeout, taking go test ./... down with a goroutine dump instead of a diff

classify_step_type cannot use RE2: its \b is ASCII-only while Python's \w is str.isalnum() plus underscore, so 'fixé' has a word boundary after 'fix' in Go and none in CPython — implement vs general for the same step
te.get('is_error') is truthiness not `is True`; a stamp of the string 'no' is truthy in Python and a v.(bool) assertion would call the transcript clean

The [:120] and [:6] rune slices route through the shared pyval.Clip rather than becoming a seventh private clipRunes copy (six already exist across scans, graduation, playbook, evolver, skills/utility, director)
